note: Single source of truth for mikedesign. Adding a tell here makes every command inherit it. Severity 'hard' gates a result; 'advisory' is reported for judgment and never blocks. Scope 'rendered' needs computed styles collected from a real browser; 'text' runs on visible text from either source.

budgets._note: Word ceilings by surface type. 'read' surfaces (docs, legal, articles) deliberately have no body ceiling. Override per project in the DESIGN.md config block.

budgetSeverity._note: Overflow on the compressible roles gates. Prose is reported, because a legitimate long paragraph is a judgment call.
budgetSeverity.headline: hard
budgetSeverity.caption: hard

rules.title: Indigo/violet default palette
rules.why: The single most-cited AI tell. Tailwind's indigo-500 default leaked into a generation of generated interfaces, so this hue band now reads as 'nobody chose this'.
rules.fix: Pick a hue from the brief, the product, or the use scene. If the brand really is violet, declare it in the DESIGN.md palette and this stops firing.

rules.title: Gradient applied to text
rules.why: Decoration standing in for hierarchy, and a reliable generated-page marker.
rules.fix: Emphasis comes from weight, size, or space.

rules.title: Eyebrow / kicker label above a heading
rules.why: A small uppercase label announcing the section the heading is about to name. Pure filler; the heading already carries its own weight.
rules.fix: Delete it. If it holds real information, fold that into the heading.

rules.title: Emoji standing in for an icon system
rules.why: Emoji render differently on every platform, cannot inherit stroke weight or colour, and signal that no icon decision was made.
rules.fix: Draw the icon, or use one real library at a consistent stroke and weight.

rules.title: Zero-offset glow used as depth
rules.why: A shadow with no offset is a coloured halo, not depth. Real depth implies a light source, so it has direction.
rules.fix: Give the shadow an offset and a soft blur, or remove it.

rules.title: Unspecified default typeface as the display voice
rules.why: Inter and the platform sans are what you get when nobody chose a typeface. On a display element that absence is visible.
rules.fix: Source and self-host a face whose character matches the brief, then declare it in the DESIGN.md fonts block.

rules.title: Fabricated testimonial or attribution
rules.why: Invented people presented as real customers. Beyond being a tell, it is a claim you cannot stand behind.
rules.fix: Use a real quote with a real name, or cut the section until you have one.

rules.title: Round invented metric presented as fact
rules.why: '10,000+ happy customers' and '99.9% uptime' with nothing behind them. An invented number reads as a real claim.
rules.fix: Use a measured number, or make the point without one.

rules.title: Em dash in interface copy
rules.why: One of the most reliable machine-written markers, and against house style.
rules.fix: Restructure with commas, colons, parentheses, or two sentences.

rules.title: Pure #ffffff or #000000 as the page ground
rules.why: Measured across a set of well-regarded software marketing sites, not one uses either. They sit on warm off-whites and blue-cast near-blacks (#FFFFEB, #FCF9F8, #05080F). Pure values are the untouched default, and they read as one.
rules.fix: Warm or cool the ground a few points toward the brand. It costs nothing and it is the difference between a chosen ground and no ground.

rules.title: Transition on a property that forces layout
rules.why: Animating width, height, top, left, margin or padding re-runs layout every frame and drops frames on cheap hardware. The reference sites animate almost nothing else but opacity and transform: 656 of 831 transition declarations on one, 319 of 305 on another.
rules.fix: Move it to transform and opacity. Scale instead of width, translate instead of top.

rules.title: Row of near-identical icon + heading + text cards
rules.why: The default page scaffold when no structure was chosen. Cards are the lazy container.
rules.fix: Let the content decide the structure. Different things should look different.

rules.title: Backdrop blur used as decoration
rules.why: Glass is a specific effect for layering over content. Applied to a static panel it is costume.
rules.fix: Keep it only where something actually shows through and moves behind it.

rules.title: Blurred gradient orb behind the hero
rules.why: Atmosphere applied because the hero felt empty, not because the design called for it.
rules.fix: Fill the hero with the product, the proof, or nothing.

rules.title: Decorative 01 / 02 / 03 section numbers
rules.fix: Keep the numbers only when the reader must follow them in order.

rules.title: Filler phrasing that carries no information
rules.why: Sentences shaped like value propositions that say nothing specific about this product.
rules.fix: Say the concrete thing the product does, in the product's own language.

rules.title: Dark theme as a default reflex
rules.why: Dark is a decision from the use scene (who, where, ambient light), not a category habit. Chosen by reflex it is the most common single tell.
rules.fix: Justify it from the use scene in DESIGN.md, or start light.

rules.title: Monospace used to signal 'technical'
rules.why: Monospace is for code, data, and measurement. Elsewhere it is a costume.
rules.fix: Use the body face, and let the content carry the credibility.

rules.title: Rule-of-three phrasing
rules.why: 'Faster, simpler, and smarter.' A rhythm models reach for when there is nothing specific to say.
rules.fix: Keep the one claim that is true and specific. Cut the two that pad the rhythm.
